quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 40 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: As you approach a blind intersection, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: In the part of the lane where other drivers can see you easiest.
In the part of the lane closest to the traffic control device.
On the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the part of the lane where other drivers can see you easiest.
questions.explanation: Position your motorcycle so other drivers can see you as early as possible at a blind intersection.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash?

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet that is fastened securely is the single most important action you can take to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: Another driver may need your lane to pass.
You may be hidden in the vehicle's blind spot.
You will have better access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be hidden in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. The vehicle could also block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen in daylight, you should:

options.text: Not wear bright clothing during the day.
Wear bright clothing during the day.
Wear dark clothing during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing during the day.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright clothing when riding to make yourself more visible to other drivers, even during the day.

questions.question: How should you brake on a motorcycle?

options.text: Apply the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Using only the rear brake can prevent you from developing the skill to use the front brake when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: What color are service signs?
questions.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters. They show where you can find rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: What should you wear to improve your chances of surviving a crash?
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards gives you the best head and neck protection. A properly fastened, quality helmet is the most effective way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT part of a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: A pre-ride inspection should check the tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, chassis, and stands. Paint inspection is not necessary.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A stop sign is coming ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is coming ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns you that a stop sign is ahead.

questions.question: When riding over grooved pavement in a work zone, what should you do?

options.text: Look down to watch the road surface.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Move to the edge of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up when riding through a work zone. Ride slowly over the grooved pavement.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head, shoulders, and torso.

questions.explanation: Turn only your head when looking through a turn. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a way to maintain control of a motorcycle in a turn?
questions.explanation: To stay in control during a turn, slow down before entering it. Look through the turn in the direction you want to go. Lean your motorcycle by pressing the handle grip. Gradually speed up through the turn to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop your motorcycle until the dog loses interest.
Approach the dog slowly, then quickly speed up as it gets close.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the dog slowly, then quickly speed up as it gets close.
questions.explanation: If a dog approaches your motorcycle, slow down and downshift. When the dog gets close, quickly speed up and move away from it.

questions.question: Taking over-the-counter medicine before riding:

options.text: Is usually fine because over-the-counter medicines are weak.
May affect your riding and should be done carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: May affect your riding and should be done carefully.
questions.explanation: Many medicines, including over-the-counter ones, can affect your ability to ride safely. Talk to your doctor about how new medicine may affect your riding.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle starts moving.
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it space and go slowly. Be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: Wind noise:

options.text: Is easy to get used to.

questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise can cause permanent hearing damage. Wear ear plugs or other hearing protection when riding.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, the effects:

options.text: Are less dangerous than when used alone.
Can be stronger than when used alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be stronger than when used alone.
questions.explanation: Many medicines can make riding unsafe. Some become even more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster your body removes it.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the faster alcohol builds up in your body. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink in an hour, alcohol will still be in your system after an hour.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the formation you should use:
questions.explanation: Groups usually ride in a staggered formation. Switch to single-file when taking curves, making turns, entering or leaving highways.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection:

options.text: Should only be done by a certified mechanic.

questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. A pre-ride inspection usually takes just a few minutes.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: You can go through the intersection carefully.
You must let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop and wait for a green signal that allows you to turn in the direction you want.

questions.question: To make a quick turn, you should:
questions.explanation: To turn quickly, make your motorcycle lean fast in the direction you want to go. The sharper the turn, the more the motorcycle must lean.

questions.question: When turning, what should you do?

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head to look through the turn.
Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon. Turning your shoulders can make you steer off course.

questions.question: Which factor affects a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: how much alcohol was consumed, how fast it was consumed, and the person's body weight.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear reflective clothing to be more visible, even during daylight. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs.

questions.question: The oily strip in the center of a lane:

options.text: Should only be used if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.
Usually has good traction, unless it is raining.
Should be avoided at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually has good traction, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The center strip is usually oily but provides enough grip for riding in dry conditions. When it rains, traction is reduced. The strip is usually about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing down or stopping. Using both brakes helps you stop quickly.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a rider should NOT:

options.text: Choose a lane position that makes them more visible.
Speed up to cross the intersection faster.
Cover the clutch and brakes to react faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection faster.
questions.explanation: When approaching an intersection, pick a lane position where other drivers can see you. Be ready to brake and use the clutch to slow your reaction time. Slow down. Do not change speed or position suddenly because other drivers may misunderstand your actions.

questions.question: You are most likely to have a collision:
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts between motorcycles and other traffic happen.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, the following distance should:
questions.explanation: A motorcycle towing a trailer needs a longer following distance. The extra weight means the motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: When someone is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Change lanes to let them pass, or slow down to create more space in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them pass, or slow down to create more space in front of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: When someone tailgates you, ride in a way that encourages them to pass. Speeding up only makes them tailgate at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What should riders know about blind spots on motorcycles?

options.text: They are nothing to worry about.
They don't exist if the motorcycle has a rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your normal riding routine.

questions.question: Are motorcycle helmets required?
questions.explanation: In Georgia, you must wear a U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet every time you operate a motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: How should a group of riders ride together?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. It keeps riders close together while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file when taking curves, turning, entering highways, or exiting highways.

questions.question: When someone is passing you on the left, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the right portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed on your left. Riding on the right side is dangerous because it may encourage the passing driver to return to your lane too quickly.

questions.question: Your motorcycle is weaving while riding over bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross the surface faster.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight across the gratings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across the gratings.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves over bridge gratings, maintain a steady speed and go straight across. Do not zigzag to stay in your lane, as this is dangerous.

questions.question: How do you shift to a higher gear on a motorcycle?

options.text: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift it.
Place your foot over the shift lever and push it.
Use your thumb to move the lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift it.
questions.explanation: To shift to a higher gear, put your foot under the shift lever and lift it up.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the roadway is divided ahead.
